status: Independently implemented and reproduced; assumed mechanism, not empirical user data
note: Illustrative model reproduced for this edition, not fitted to a real platform. Four conditions each use 400 runs of 5,000 recommendations, eight baseline click probabilities 0.20, 0.19, …, 0.13, and estimates starting at one click in five showings. The feed either chooses its highest estimated rate (random ties) or explores uniformly with probability 0.10. In the habit condition a click raises that topic's probability by 1% of its remaining distance to 0.60; after each round all probabilities relax 0.05% toward their baselines. The leading topic is the most shown in the last 1,000 rounds. Without habit it was the original favorite in 26.5% of greedy runs and 53.0% of exploratory runs; with habit, 21.5% and 22.5%. For the greedy habit condition its mean click probability rose from 0.174 to 0.565. Curves select that leading topic retrospectively and average across runs. Python standard-library implementation; master seed 20261119, incremented by run. Reinforcement, decay and click-as-preference are modeling choices, not empirical estimates; clicks do not establish welfare. Reproduction code and data are retained with the editorial source materials.
